question: As per census 2011, which of the following states has the highest scheduled caste population?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The 2011 Census of India provided detailed data on the population of Scheduled Castes (SCs) across the country.
 
• Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest absolute number of Scheduled Caste individuals.
 
• The large population of Uttar Pradesh contributes to this high number.
 
• The state has a long history of social stratification and caste-based discrimination.
 
• The Scheduled Caste population in Uttar Pradesh is spread across various districts.
 
• The census data includes information on the distribution of SCs in rural and urban areas.
 
• The government of India has implemented various programs and policies to uplift the Scheduled Caste communities.
 
• These programs aim to provide access to education, employment, and social justice.
 
• The census data is used to inform policy decisions and allocate resources for SC welfare.
 
• The percentage of SC population relative to the total population of a state is a different metric than the total number of SC individuals.
 
• While Uttar Pradesh has the largest absolute number, other states may have a higher percentage of SCs in their population.
 
• The census also provides information on the literacy rates and work participation rates of Scheduled Castes.
 
• This data helps to assess the socio-economic conditions of SC communities.
 
• The government of India uses the census data to determine the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes in educational institutions and government jobs.
 
• The constitution of India provides for the protection of the scheduled castes.
 
• The census data is crucial for monitoring the progress of SC communities over time.
 
• The data also helps to identify areas where targeted interventions are needed.
 
• The census data is used by researchers and social scientists to study caste dynamics in India.
 
• The information allows social scientists to understand the demographics of the population.
 
• The census information is also used to determine political boundaries.
